description: Graphs that teach > graphs that impress. Turn any code into an interactive knowledge graph you can explore, search, and ask questions about. Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot, Gemini CLI, and more.
summary: I like that this treats code comprehension as a graph problem rather than a "summarize the README" problem — the multi-agent pipeline walks every file, function, and dependency, then hands you a navigable structure you can search semantically and trace diff impact through before you commit. It slots naturally next to PenguPool in my setup: one routes the agent sessions, the other makes what those sessions actually understand visible and inspectable. The "graphs that teach, not impress" framing is the right altitude for a tool whose job is to kill the 200k-line onboarding tax, not add another dashboard to admire.
